sections.text:
Ruth is a short story set in the time of the judges. Ruth, a widow from Moab, refuses to leave her mother-in-law Naomi and travels with her to Bethlehem. Gleaning in the fields to find food, she meets Boaz, a relative of Naomi’s husband.

Boaz acts as the family’s redeemer and marries Ruth. Their son Obed becomes the grandfather of King David.

The story depends on two customs of ancient Israel: the right of the poor to gather what harvesters left behind, and the duty of a near relative to protect a family’s land and name. When the book was written is debated; proposals range from the early monarchy to the time after the exile.

Readers have long loved this book for its picture of loyal love between ordinary people, and of God’s care working quietly through everyday choices. It matters that Ruth is a foreigner who is welcomed among God’s people. Matthew names her in the family line of Jesus.
